name: Catalytic reforming (CCR, semi-regenerative)
principle: Hydrotreated heavy naphtha passes over a platinum (or platinum-rhenium) catalyst in a series of reactors with fired heaters between them, because the reactions absorb heat. Naphthenes and paraffins become aromatics and hydrogen. Semi-regenerative units stop every 8 to 18 months to regenerate catalyst; continuous units circulate catalyst through a regenerator.

source.note: US EPA AP-42 Section 5.1 Petroleum Refining (April 2015 revision), process descriptions

reference_plants.name: Sinopec Hainan Petrochemical (200th UOP CCR Platforming unit)
reference_plants.capacity: not stated; CCR Platforming first commercialised 1971

limitations: Catalyst sensitive to sulfur and nitrogen
